samples.summary: Cell-aware copy resolves against `getLayout()` (body) instead of `getActiveLayout()`, so the #872 fix does not apply to tables in the header/footer
samples.evidence: `getSelectedBlocks()` still starts with `const layout = this.getLayout();` and then does `layout.blockParentMap.get(start.blockId)`. The repo's own accessor for exactly this lookup is `getCellInfo()` (text-editor.ts:3359-3363), which deliberately uses `this.getActiveLayout()` "so table cell editing works in every region". While `editContext` is 'header'/'footer', a selection inside a header/footer table cell is absent from the body layout's `blockParentMap` and from `layout.blocks`, so both `getNormalizedRange` and the new cell branch fail and the rich clipboard payload is empty — the same defect #872 fixes for the body. The new code had the chance to use the active layout and did not.

samples.summary: When a nested-table cell range falls through `getSelectedTableCells()`, the new cell branch can emit a bogus partial block where the old code emitted nothing
samples.evidence: `getSelectedTableCells()` resolves `cr.blockId` with `layout.blocks.find(...)` (line 3711), which returns null for a table nested inside another table, so `handleCopy`/`handleCut` fall through to `getSelectedBlocks()`. For a `tableCellRange`, `normalizeRange` returns `{start: range.anchor, end: range.focus}` *unordered* (selection.ts:123-127). Previously both `findIndex` calls in `layout.blocks` were -1 and the result was `[]`; now, if anchor and focus happen to resolve inside the same cell block list, `sliceBlockRange` slices with unordered/rectangle offsets and writes a truncated block onto the clipboard, so a paste inserts wrong content instead of falling back to plain text.

samples.summary: Context-menu Copy still keys off `getActiveSelection()` only, so it is hidden for the newly supported click-selected-image copy
samples.evidence: `const showCopy = hasSelection;` with `hasSelection = !!editor.getActiveSelection()` (line 74). `selectImageAt`/the image mousedown path call `selection.setRange(null)` (editor.ts:2507, 3643), so an image selection makes `getActiveSelection()` null. Cmd/Ctrl+C now copies the image but right-clicking it offers no Copy (and Cut is likewise hidden even though `handleCut` now supports the image case), leaving keyboard and menu inconsistent for the very case this PR adds.

samples.summary: Image copy writes an empty `text/plain` flavour, clearing the plain-text clipboard for external consumers
samples.evidence: `e.clipboardData?.setData('text/plain', image.alt ?? '')` after `preventDefault()`. Most inserted images have no `alt` (`alt?: string` in model/types.ts:133), so the copy replaces the system clipboard's text flavour with the empty string: pasting into any external app, or via the editor's own Cmd+Shift+V plain-text path, yields nothing. Writing no `text/plain` at all (or the object-replacement char) would be less destructive.

samples.summary: Shift+Delete (the Windows cut shortcut) over a selected image deletes it without ever writing the clipboard
samples.evidence: The new copy/cut absorption only matches `mod && (key==='c'||key==='x')`. Shift+Delete falls to `if (key === 'Delete' || key === 'Backspace')`, which `preventDefault()`s and calls `deleteSelectedImageInline()` — so the native `cut` event never fires and the image is destroyed with nothing on the clipboard. The mirror-image gap exists for Ctrl+Insert (copy), which lands in the catch-all and clears the image selection, reproducing #870 for that shortcut.

samples.summary: Image cut deletes the image even when `clipboardData` is unavailable
samples.evidence: `this.writeImageToClipboard(e, selected.image)` uses `e.clipboardData?.setData(...)`; if `clipboardData` is null the writes are silently skipped, yet `this.imageDeleteHandler?.()` on the next line removes the image regardless — content destroyed with nothing on the clipboard. (The text cut path has the same shape, so this is a propagated rather than novel pattern; undo still recovers it.)
